title: Domino's Garlic Bread Twists
description: Eight lengths of baked dough brushed with garlic and butter-flavoured seasoning, served with marinara — the plainest bread side Domino's makes.
fullContent:
The Plain One

Eight lengths of bread dough, twisted, baked, and brushed with garlic and a butter-flavoured seasoning, served with a marinara cup. This is the most straightforward side Domino's makes — no filling, no cheese layer, no surprises. Garlic bread in a twisted shape.

That simplicity is the appeal. It goes with everything, nobody objects to it, and it's the side you order when the pizza is already doing something interesting.

The Numbers, Including the One That Surprises People

Per 2 piecesFull 8-piece order
Calories~220~1,240
Sodium~220mg~1,520mg
Fat~11g~62g
Protein~5g~32g

The per-serving figure of 220 looks modest, and that's how most people think about it. The full order at around 1,240 calories is the number that matters, and it's larger than anything else in the side category — more than a Chicken Bacon Ranch sandwich at ~870, and more than half a large cheese pizza.

Sodium follows the same pattern: ~1,520mg across the order is roughly two thirds of a day's suggested limit.

None of that makes it a bad item. It makes it a course rather than a side, and the practical consequence is simple — shared between three or four people alongside a pizza it's entirely reasonable, and eaten by one person as an accompaniment it isn't.

Garlic or Parmesan?

Domino's makes two twist varieties and they're the same dough with a different finish.

  • Garlic Bread Twists — seasoning and butter flavour, ~220 per two pieces
  • Parmesan Bread Twists — cheese added on top, ~230 per two pieces

Ten calories apart, normally identical in price. So this is purely taste, and the useful rule is about what else you've ordered: garlic is the better partner for a pizza that already has a lot going on, and Parmesan is better when the bread is doing more of the work in the meal.

If you've ordered a Parmesan Stuffed Crust pizza, garlic twists are the sensible choice — otherwise you're having the same garlic-Parmesan finish twice in one meal.

Twists or Bites?

The real decision in this category, and it comes down to arithmetic rather than flavour.

Garlic Bread TwistsParmesan Bread Bites
Pieces816
Example price~$5.99~$4.99
Cost per piece~75¢~31¢
Best forDipping, eating as a sideSharing around a table

The bites are cheaper and divide better; the twists are more substantial and dip better. Eight twists among four people is two each and immediately awkward if someone wants a third. Sixteen bites among four is four each, and nobody has to be polite about it.

Order twists when it's one or two of you and you want something to dip. Order bites when it's a table.

The Dip Does Real Work

The twists are deliberately plain, which makes the dipping cup more important here than on a seasoned side. It also has a calorie cost people don't count:

  • Marinara — around 45 calories a cup, and normally included
  • Ranch or blue cheese — roughly 100 to 170 a cup
  • Garlic and butter style dips — the heaviest of the lot

Two or three creamy cups across a shared order adds as much as a couple of extra twists would. Marinara is the free option in calorie terms, and it suits garlic bread better than a creamy dip does anyway.

Who It Suits

  • Two or three people sharing alongside a pizza
  • Anyone who wants plain garlic bread rather than a cheese-filled side
  • Dipping — the twist shape holds sauce far better than small bites do
  • Reheating — nothing in them splits or sets, so leftovers come back well in an oven

And who it doesn't:

  • Bigger groups — sixteen bites divide better than eight twists
  • One person adding a side to a pizza — a full order is a lot of bread for one
  • Vegans — all Domino's bread sides contain milk
  • Anyone avoiding gluten

Ordering Them Well

  • Build them into a deal. Bread sides are usually Mix & Match eligible, and adding one at the end at menu price is the expensive route — our deal comparison covers which offer fits which basket
  • Let them replace pizza rather than accompany it. A full order plus a full pizza per person is a great deal of bread in one meal
  • Eat them hot. They firm up as they cool more noticeably than most items here
  • Check what your pizza already has. Garlic on garlic is a common accidental order

Where They Sit

Against the other bread sides, these are the middle option — cheaper and lighter than Stuffed Cheesy Bread, more substantial and better for dipping than the bites, and plainer than either.

Against the wider menu, they're the most reliable side on it. Nothing about them depends on timing, temperature or a specific taste. That's not exciting, but on a menu where several items are genuinely worse after a long delivery, being unremarkable is a real advantage.

title: Domino's Loaded Tots
description: Crispy potato tots baked with cheese and toppings in three versions — the only non-bread hot side Domino's makes, and the one most damaged by a long delivery.
fullContent:
The Only Non-Bread Hot Side

Loaded Tots are the newest addition to this part of Domino's menu, and the only hot side that isn't bread or chicken: crispy potato tots baked with sauce and cheese on top, in three versions.

That alone is most of the reason to order them. Until they arrived, adding something hot to a Domino's order meant bread, more bread, or wings.

The Three Versions

VersionWhat's on themPer ¼Full order
Cheddar BaconBacon, mozzarella, cheddar, garlic Parmesan sauce~240 cal~960 cal
Melty 3-CheeseMozzarella, cheddar, provolone, Alfredo~210 cal~840 cal
Philly Cheese SteakSteak, onions, green peppers, Alfredo, cheese blend~200 cal~800 cal

All three are normally the same price, commonly around $6.99 inside a Mix & Match style order.

Worth noticing: Philly Cheese Steak is both the lightest and the one with the most actual filling. If you're choosing on merit rather than on how much cheese is visible, that's the pick. Cheddar Bacon is the most popular and the richest; Melty 3-Cheese is the simplest and the only meat-free option.

The Sodium Figure

The number that doesn't appear anywhere a customer will see it.

Cheddar Bacon carries roughly 590mg of sodium per quarter portion, which puts a full order near 2,360mg — above the 2,300mg daily limit US dietary guidelines suggest for an adult. The other two versions sit a little lower, around 2,040 to 2,120mg for a full order, which is still most of a day.

Shared between three or four people alongside a pizza, that's a normal portion of a normal meal. Eaten by one person as a side, it's a day's sodium in something described as an accompaniment. That's worth knowing rather than worrying about — but it's the kind of thing that only shows up if someone goes looking.

The Delivery Problem

This is the single most useful thing on this page, and it decides whether you enjoy them.

Crispness is the entire point of a tot, and steam destroys it. Sealed in a container with hot cheese on top, moisture has nowhere to go but back into the potato. Twenty minutes later you have warm, soft potato under cheese — perfectly edible, and not what you ordered.

  • Carryout: genuinely good — crisp outside, molten on top
  • Short delivery: fine
  • Long delivery: soft, and you'll wonder what the fuss was about

Loaded Tots and lava cakes are the only two items on the Domino's menu that are structurally different after a long drive rather than just cooler. Everything else arrives less hot; these arrive changed.

So the rule is simple: if your store is far away, order bread instead and save the tots for a pickup run. Our carryout guide covers where pickup wins on price too, which makes that an easy trade rather than a sacrifice.

How They Taste

Familiar, in a good way — these are recognisably potato tots rather than a reinvention, and that's the right call. What differentiates them is the sauce underneath the cheese:

  • Garlic Parmesan on the Cheddar Bacon gives it a savoury, garlicky edge
  • Alfredo on the other two is creamier and milder

None of the three is spicy. If you were hoping for heat, there isn't any in this part of the menu.

Who It Suits

  • Carryout orders — the format they're actually built for
  • Anyone bored of bread sides, which until recently was the only real option
  • Sharing between two or three — a portion divides into about four servings
  • Children — familiar, mild, easy to eat

And who it doesn't:

  • Long-delivery orders — the one situation where they genuinely disappoint
  • Vegans — all three versions carry dairy
  • Vegetarians wanting choice — only Melty 3-Cheese qualifies
  • Anyone watching sodium — a full order is around a day's worth

Ordering Them Well

  • Take them on carryout. This matters more here than for any other side on the menu
  • Build them into a deal — the ~$6.99 price generally comes from Mix & Match style pricing; standalone they cost more
  • Don't stack them with a bread side. Both are heavy starch, and one is plenty alongside pizza
  • Eat them first if they arrive with a pizza — they're the most time-sensitive thing in the bag
  • Check availability — as a newer item, not every store carries all three versions

Where They Sit

Against the bread sides, tots are the change of pace — different texture, different format, and the only thing in this category that isn't dough. They cost a little more than Parmesan Bread Bites and about the same as garlic twists.

Against the wider menu, they're the clearest example of an item where how you order matters more than what you order. The same tots are a good side or a mediocre one depending entirely on the distance between you and the store — which is a more interesting fact about them than anything in the recipe.
